output.normalized_title: search-indexer: LDAP sync daemon timeout after 30000ms (search-indexer)

output.classification_reasoning: The failure originates from the LDAP synchronization daemon within the search-indexer service timing out after 30 seconds. LDAP is an authentication directory service, and a timeout indicates that the indexer could not successfully communicate with the authentication backend, leading to degraded functionality and a telemetry spike. The issue involves external directory integration, timeout handling, and service coordination, which introduces more than trivial troubleshooting steps but does not require a full system redesign, placing the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
Kubectl context set to production cluster
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Current incident shares the same service and secondary telemetry spike with INC-1004, but the symptom (LDAP sync timeout) and error signature differ. The pattern suggests a possible authentication-related degradation rather than the prior network failure.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident affects 3,500 users, which exceeds the cross‑tier impact threshold of 2,000 users defined in the SLA rule. Although the service tier is Tier‑3, the rule applies across tiers when the user count surpasses 2,000. The outage duration of 17 minutes is well within typical response windows for SEV‑2 incidents, and the correlated context indicates a new authentication‑related degradation rather than a higher‑priority network failure. Therefore, the deterministic rule mandates a SEV‑2 classification.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Cluster Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required ProdOperations role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster.
verification: AWS identity ARN matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context name contains 'prod' or matches expected cluster identifier

remediation_steps.title: Confirm Write‑Freeze State and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Check that a write‑freeze is in place to avoid data loss, then promote the healthy read‑replica to primary before any node restarts.
commands: kubectl get configmap write-freeze -n infra -o jsonpath='{.data.status}'
verification: Write‑freeze configmap reports status=enabled
Promotion script returns success and new primary reports role=primary

remediation_steps.title: Restart LDAP Sync Daemon Pods
remediation_steps.description: Perform a rolling restart of the LDAP sync daemon to clear the 30‑second timeout deadlock.
verification: All ldap-sync-daemon pods reach READY=1/1 and status=Running
Log stream shows no timeout errors for at least 5 minutes

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Validate that the search‑indexer service and authentication pathways are healthy after the daemon restart.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=search-indexer -n search --tail=100 | grep -i error
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body containing 'status":"OK'
No error lines related to LDAP or authentication appear in recent logs
Service endpoint resolves and responds within latency SLA

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the LDAP sync daemon deployment to its previous image tag, demote the promoted replica if needed, and lift the write‑freeze only after confirming stability.

steps.description: Undo LDAP sync daemon rollout to previous container image
verification: Pods restart with previous image tag and reach READY=1/1
Timeout errors reappear in logs (used as a diagnostic indicator that rollback occurred)

steps.description: Demote the promoted read‑replica back to secondary if the primary remains healthy
verification: Original primary reports role=primary again
New replica reports role=replica
Configmap status now reads 'disabled'
No new write‑freeze alerts in monitoring

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations role
Rollback procedures documented in runbook RB-110
Write‑freeze status confirmed before any node or pod restarts
Current deployment image tags recorded for audit
